title: design.submit and design.read are published and reachable by a seat
description:
SPIDR child 1b of task-8a6d6660c31c4e119f962d13e6f1505d, split out by architect-20a6d1eb 2026-09-05 when child 1a's roster measured 11 distinct files against the 10-file hard cap. Cut along the INTERFACE axis: task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a owns the CONTRACT and the versioned AGGREGATE; this row PUBLISHES the two kinds and makes them reachable.

dependsOn task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a - the kinds dispatch into its store.

THESE ARE SEAT KINDS, THE EXCEPTION ON THIS BOARD. Every other kind this epic adds is human-only and MCP-EXCLUDED. `design.submit` is submitted BY AN AGENT and `design.read` is read by seats AND the operator, so both must be REACHABLE over MCP. Copying the approval.decide / escalation.decide pattern here would make the design step unstaffable while looking correct in review - that is the single most likely failure of this row.

THE TWO KINDS TAKE DIFFERENT ROUTES TO BEING SERVED, measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04):
- `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:87-89` builds the served set as ALL command kinds MINUS `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` (:59), PLUS `MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS` (:27). So `design.submit`, being a COMMAND, is served by simply NOT being added to the exclusion roster - there is no positive action, and the mistake would be adding it there out of habit.
- `design.read` is a QUERY: it must be ADDED to `MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS` (:27, beside product_contract.read, graph.get, events.read, documents.source_read) AND given a handler in the dispatch map at `mcp-dispatch-port.ts:302` (`"product_contract.read": answerProductContractRead` is the shape). A query in the roster with no handler advertises a capability the port cannot serve.

DAEMON ROSTER: daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (kind, capability, family, PAYLOAD_KEYS), daemon-command-families.ts (the per-kind flag block :83-94), daemon-command-registry.ts (`entryOf` :205-212). TWO PAYLOAD-KEY TEST TABLES must both gain rows and are invisible to a grep for the kind literal: daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts (~:170-182) and daemon-command-registry.test.ts (~:197-203 plus the flat roster ~:283-300).

THE SHARED CONTRACT AND THE GENERATED CLIENT (packages/contracts runtime-vocabulary + `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`) are needed only when the BROWSER must dispatch these kinds. The operator reads the design through child 3's screen; decide at plan time whether that needs the generated client, and if so include it - never hand-edit it, since it pins GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST checked at client-compat.ts:169.
definitionOfDone: `design.submit` and `design.read` are published across the daemon roster (vocabulary kind/capability/family/PAYLOAD_KEYS, families flag, registry entry) with a BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality test enumerating the SERVED kinds from the dispatch seam; verify by deleting each entry from each side in turn and confirming all four deletions go red.

BOTH ARE SEAT-REACHABLE OVER MCP, asserted behaviourally rather than by roster membership: an AGENT-authenticated dispatch of `design.submit` REACHES the handler, and an agent-authenticated `design.read` returns its answer. This is the opposite of every other kind this epic adds, and the arm exists because copying the human-only pattern would make the design step unstaffable while passing review.
`design.submit` is NOT in `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` and NOT in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS - assert both absences explicitly, since each is a place a well-meaning worker would add it by habit.

`design.read` is in `MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS` (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:27) AND has a handler in the dispatch map (mcp-dispatch-port.ts:302 area). Assert BOTH: a query advertised without a handler promises a capability the port cannot serve, and the allowlist's own parity test compares the roster against the port's table.

Both payload-key TEST tables gain their rows (daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts and daemon-command-registry.test.ts, including its flat kind roster) - these are invisible to a grep for the kind literal in production source and have cost this board a rejected plan before.

If the browser must dispatch either kind, packages/contracts' runtime vocabulary and the REGENERATED client move with it (`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`, quoting the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST). If it need not, say so explicitly in the record rather than leaving it ambiguous for child 3.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, plus `pnpm test` if packages/ was touched.
taskRails: SEAT KINDS, NOT HUMAN GATES. Do not add `design.submit` to MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS or HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. The surrounding pattern invites exactly that mistake and it would silently make the design step unstaffable.
A SERVED QUERY NEEDS BOTH a roster entry and a dispatch handler. One without the other is an advertised capability the port cannot serve.
NO AGGREGATE WORK: the contract and the versioned store are task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a's. No wrapper, no mission, no UI.
NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client; run the generator and quote both digests.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

(1) THE COMMAND HALF. The plan says "keep the addition small and reformat nothing" in a file already at 509 lines / 400-line bar, so the edge is its OWN module (+ `.js` bridge), exactly as `daemon-command-environment.ts` is: NEW `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-design.ts` (113 lines) exporting `runDesignSubmitEdge`, plus 25 lines in the registry (import, `design` in the `commandFamilyFacts` destructure, one dispatch branch).   REFUSALS GO THROUGH THE SLICE'S CLOSED MAP AND NOWHERE ELSE. The edge's only `refuse()` builds `DomainRefusal(refusal.code, refusal.layer, detail)` from a `DesignRefusal` that `designRefusal(code)` minted, and `designRefusal` reads the layer out of `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` — so NO LAYER LITERAL APPEARS AT ANY THROW SITE and no code/layer pair can disagree. No new `*_LAYER` constant, so no boundary-roster backfill. The store's refusals travel UNRESTAMPED (code, layer, sourceCode, sourceLayer preserved): re-wrapping would report a CONTRACT_AUTHORITY verdict as a REQUEST fault. Only one refusal is minted here — a non-string/empty `goalRef` takes DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID @ REQUEST, the same code `decodeDesignRevision` answers with, rather than a fifth code.

  AUTHORITY FIELDS ARE SERVER FACTS: projectId + principalId from the authenticated principal, commandId/correlationId/expectedVersion from the envelope, decidedAt from `clock`. A fenced submit is RETURNED not thrown by the store, so the edge branches on `result.ok` — "it did not throw" is not treated as success.
